segments.t: Armed with a kitchen knife just in case, Senya and Fedya creep out to the courtyard to scare the photographer sitting in a car outside the restaurant. The plan goes horribly wrong when Fedya panics during the confrontation and accidentally knocks the man out cold.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'We will just scare him a little, right?' Kostya checks quietly to see how Nastya will answer on the spot.
'What do you need this knife for?' Emphasizing the knife in front of Kostya, Nastya uses "nozh" ("knife") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'Just in case.' Discussing the case beside Nastya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?
'In case you suddenly need to slice some bread?' Nastya wonders wryly if there is more going on behind the scenes.

'We agreed we are only going to scare him.' Kostya steps in dryly beside Nastya and reaches for the Russian word "dogovorili" ("to finish speaking", built from "dogovorit") right at the center of the line.
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.
'Go on, you go ahead and I will keep watch.' Bringing up the joke in front of Kostya, Nastya starts with "davay" ("come on, let's") to invite Kostya right into the action.
'It is nothing, come on, get going.' Kostya pushes back pointedly facing Nastya, before Nastya can change the subject.
'Guys, what on earth is going on?' Underscoring the boys with Kostya, Nastya uses "proiskhodit" ("is going on") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'Keep quiet, keep quiet, hush!' Kostya fires back right away with a smile, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'What have you done?' Nastya wonders firmly what Kostya is actually getting at here.
'I just wanted to scare him a little.' Kostya proceeds candidly right here and brings in "pripugnut" ("to scare a little") to make the meaning unmistakable.
'Why did you even touch him at all?' Leaning in calmly around Kostya, Nastya drops in "voobshche" ("in general, altogether") to sum up the whole situation at once.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?
'Listen, why on earth did I go with you?' Kostya questions frankly what Nastya is actually getting at here.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?
That wraps up this scene as senya and Fedya sneak out to intimidate the man sitting in a parked car outside Claude Monet, but Fedya accidentally knocks him unconscious. See you next time!
